title: Projects
text:
Investigating the gap between true scores and observed scores in the measurement of psychological processes: A formal theory of scaling
Currently, I am working on my master’s thesis, which is a blend of methodology and psychology. The aim of this project is to formulate a theory of the scaling mechanism and formalize it (basically, write it out in a programming language). A lot of psychological research is conducted using questionnaires for data collection. Participants filling them out must interpret the items, recall relevant information, aggregate it into a final judgement and transfer it onto the available response format. I am interested in the last part which I refer to as the scaling mechanism - the mapping of the internal judgement onto the scale.

title: About
text: I hold a bachelor’s degree in psychology from the University of Ljubljana, Slovenia. During my studies, I was part of the PR group of the Slovenian Psychology Students’ Association (DŠPS). Our goal was to make psychology accessible by creating fun and informative posts about various psychological topics. I took an extra year to explore my interests, during which I wrote and published two papers.

title: About
text:
Currently
I’m currently in my second year of my research master’s programme in Methodology, Statistics and Data Science at Utrecht University. Most of my time is spent working on my thesis, aiming to uncover the hidden processes behind responding to psychological questionnaire items.

title: About
text:
Outside academia
When I’m not at my desk doing university work, I like to switch between reading thrillers and my various creative hobbies, from painting and experimenting with vocal harmonies to creating fun makeup looks, crocheting, playing guitar, and many more. With so many to choose from, none of these hobbies gets much of my attention, but I enjoy returning to them every once in a while.
